newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No frost seen in Brazil coffee areas for now-Somar.
newsitem.headline: No frost seen in Brazil coffee areas for now-Somar.

text.p: A cold front is forecast to reach southern Brazil by the end of next week, but it was likely not to reach coffee producing regions and it was too early to predict frost, independent meteorologist Somar said. "According to what we are seeing, there is no possibility of frost," said Somar forecaster Marcio Custodio.
The weather was set to remain sunny this week, with rain arriving in the coffee regions on August 5.
"Afterwards, there is a mass of cold air but it is very far south. It shouldn't reach the coffee belt but it is very early to be certain," Custodio said.
The cold front was currently over the Pacific, south of Argentina, he said.
Weather forecaster Cropcast earlier said long-range guidance models showed there was a 15 percent chance of frost in Brazil's coffee producing areas on the weekend of August 9 and 10.
But Weather Services Corp meteorologist Mike Palmerino warned long-range weather models could be highly unreliable.
"For the moment, for the next seven days there is no chance of frost whatsoever," said Custodio, adding that it was difficult to make predicitons beyond a seven to 10 day outlook.
